title: Sarojini Naidu's birth chart
metaDescription: Sarojini Naidu's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 24.2° Aquarius. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The chart's headline is a square: the Sun and Pluto within 0.3°, identity wired to depth. A square is the tradition’s engine room: two drives at cross purposes, and the friction is the horsepower.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun sits at 24.2° Aquarius — the third decan, 20°–30°, which the tradition sub-rules by Venus. Degrees matter more than the sign label here: two people born a fortnight apart share Aquarius and share almost nothing else about where the Sun actually stood.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: The personal planets sit Mercury at 10.1° Aquarius, Venus at 10.8° Pisces, Mars at 5.8° Capricorn. Mercury in an air sign reads as a mind at home in argument and pattern; Venus in a water sign reads as taste tuned to mood and undertow; Mars in an earth sign reads as drive that grinds rather than flares.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The Sun and Pluto hold the closest angle here — a square, 0.3° wide. A square is friction that produces motion — the aspect the tradition credits with building capability precisely by refusing to be comfortable. Behind it, Mars trine Neptune at 1.4°, and Mercury square Neptune at 2.9° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These are the day-proof angles — present at midnight, present at noon, present at the next midnight.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: Mars, Uranus, Neptune close a triangle of trines. Three trines close into a circuit the tradition calls a grand trine — ease so complete it can idle unnoticed for years. The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The classical table has five entries for this chart. The Sun in Aquarius at 24.2° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; the Moon in Scorpio at 17.6° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Venus in Pisces at 10.8° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Mars in Capricorn at 5.8° is in exaltation; Saturn in Aries at 0.8° is in fall. The old table grades terrain, not talent — a placement in fall works uphill, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Of the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: 4 in earth, 3 in air, 2 in water, 1 in fire by element, 6 fixed, 2 mutable, 2 cardinal by modality. Earth signs hold the scheme’s slow end, where results are measured in what survives rather than what starts. Uranus was retrograde — apparent retreat against the stars, which the old reading takes as a function working from the inside first.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Scorpio for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 14.2° between midnight and midnight. The missing clock moves the Moon by half a sign at most here, and the boundary was never close. At the noon reference it stands at 17.6°.
